corpus.title: Harbour City Council: Community Grants Management System, Functional Requirements Document

arms.label: B — the whole document in one call

configuration.calls: 1 (plus one re-prompt on an unreadable reply)

requirements.text: A grants officer can create a round for a programme, recording opening and closing date and time, budget, minimum and maximum grant, eligibility questions, application questions and weighted assessment criteria.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to create a round for a programme, recording its opening and closing date and time, its budget, the minimum and maximum grant that can be requested, the eligibility questions, the application questions and the assessment criteria with their weightings.

requirements.text: A round can only be opened once its programme manager has approved its set-up, and the system records who approved it and when.
requirements.quote: A round shall only be opened once its programme manager has approved its set-up, and the system shall record who approved it and when.

requirements.text: The total budget of a programme's rounds in a financial year must not exceed the programme's budget for that year.
requirements.quote: The system shall not allow the budget of the rounds in a programme in one financial year to exceed the programme's budget for that year.

requirements.text: A grants officer can copy a previous round as the starting point for a new one.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to copy a previous round as the starting point for a new one.

requirements.text: For an invitation-only round, only invited organisations can start an application.
requirements.quote: for an invitation-only round, the system shall only let invited organisations start an application.

requirements.text: Applications are not accepted after the round's closing date and time, and an application still being completed at closing cannot be submitted.
requirements.quote: Applications shall not be accepted after a round's closing date and time, and an application that is being completed when the round closes shall not be submittable.

requirements.text: The programme manager can extend the closing date for a single applicant, recording the reason, and the extension appears in the round's audit history.
requirements.quote: The programme manager shall be able to extend the closing date for a single applicant, recording the reason, and the extension shall be shown in the round's audit history.

requirements.text: A person can register an organisation by giving name, address, legal form, charity or company number if any, and details of at least two unrelated people connected with it.
requirements.quote: A person shall be able to register an organisation in the system by giving its name, address, legal form, charity or company number if it has one, and the details of at least two people connected with it who are not related to each other.

requirements.text: A given charity or company number is checked against the public register and any difference in registered name and address is shown to the officer.
requirements.quote: Where a charity or company number is given, the system shall check it against the public register and shall show the officer any difference between the registered name and address and those entered.

requirements.text: Registration is prevented where the charity or company number is already on another organisation record, and the person is directed to request access to the existing record.
requirements.quote: The system shall prevent the registration of an organisation whose charity or company number is already held on another organisation record, and shall direct the person to request access to the existing record.

requirements.text: An organisation record can have several users, and existing users approve any request by a new user to join.
requirements.quote: An organisation record shall be able to have several users, and the organisation's existing users shall approve any request by a new user to join it.

requirements.text: If no remaining user can approve a join request, a grants officer can add a user after verifying the person's connection with the organisation.
requirements.quote: If an organisation has no remaining users who can approve a request, a grants officer shall be able to add a user after verifying the person's connection with the organisation.

requirements.text: An organisation uploads its governing document, latest accounts, safeguarding policy and equality policy once, and the system attaches the current versions to each application automatically.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall be able to upload its governing document, latest accounts, safeguarding policy and equality policy to its organisation record once, and the system shall attach the current versions to each application automatically.

requirements.text: The system records an expiry date for each organisation document and asks for a new version when one expires.
requirements.quote: The system shall record an expiry date for each organisation document and shall ask the organisation to upload a new version when one expires.

requirements.text: Accounts are treated as expired 18 months after the end of the financial year they cover.
requirements.quote: Accounts shall be treated as expired 18 months after the end of the financial year they cover.

requirements.text: Bank details are entered in the system and must be verified, with the account name matching the organisation's name via the council's verification service, before use for a payment.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall enter its bank details in the system, and the system shall verify that the account name matches the organisation's name using the council's bank account verification service before the details can be used for a payment.

requirements.text: A change of bank details takes effect only after a grants officer confirms it by telephone to a number already on the record, and the system records who called and when.
requirements.quote: A change to an organisation's bank details shall only take effect after a grants officer has confirmed it by telephone with a person connected with the organisation, using a telephone number already held on the record, and the system shall record who made the call and when.

requirements.text: No payment is released to bank details changed in the previous 10 working days until a finance officer has reviewed the change.
requirements.quote: No payment shall be released to bank details that were changed in the previous 10 working days until a finance officer has reviewed the change.

requirements.text: Before starting an application the applicant answers the eligibility questions and is told immediately whether they are eligible and, if not, which answer made them ineligible.
requirements.quote: Before starting an application, an applicant shall answer the round's eligibility questions, and the system shall tell them immediately whether they are eligible, and if not, which answer made them ineligible.

requirements.text: An ineligible applicant is shown contact details of the grants team and the local umbrella body.
requirements.quote: An applicant who is not eligible shall be shown the contact details of the grants team and of the local umbrella body that can offer advice.

requirements.text: An organisation with an overdue monitoring report on any previous grant cannot apply to a round.
requirements.quote: The system shall prevent an organisation from applying to a round if it has an overdue monitoring report on any previous grant.

requirements.text: An organisation cannot hold more than one open application to the same round.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall not hold more than one open application to the same round.

requirements.text: The application form saves answers automatically and the applicant can leave and return at any time before the round closes.
requirements.quote: The application form shall save the applicant's answers automatically as they are entered, and the applicant shall be able to leave and return to the application at any time before the round closes.

requirements.text: Several users of an organisation can work on an application but only one can edit at a time, and the system shows who is editing.
requirements.quote: Several users of the same organisation shall be able to work on an application, but only one shall be able to edit it at a time, and the system shall show who is editing.

requirements.text: The application has a budget table (item, cost, capital or revenue) and the system checks the total equals the amount requested.
requirements.quote: The application shall include a budget table in which the applicant lists each item of expenditure, its cost and whether it is capital or revenue, and the system shall calculate the total and check that it equals the amount requested.

requirements.text: An application cannot request less than the round's minimum or more than its maximum grant.
requirements.quote: The system shall not allow an application to request less than the round's minimum or more than its maximum grant.

requirements.text: Before submitting, the applicant confirms a declaration that the information is true, and the system records who confirmed it and when.
requirements.quote: Before submitting, the applicant shall confirm a declaration that the information given is true, and the system shall record the name of the person who confirmed it and the date and time.

requirements.text: On submission the system emails the applicant an acknowledgement with a reference number and the date a decision is expected.
requirements.quote: When an application is submitted the system shall send the applicant an acknowledgement by email with a reference number and the date by which a decision is expected.

requirements.text: A grants officer can complete and submit an application for an applicant who cannot apply online, recording this and the applicant's confirmation of the declaration.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to complete and submit an application on behalf of an applicant who cannot apply online, recording that they did so and the applicant's confirmation of the declaration.

requirements.text: The Youth Voice application form uses plain language suitable for ages 13 to 25 and lets a group of young people apply with a named adult.
requirements.quote: The Youth Voice fund application form shall use plain language suitable for applicants aged 13 to 25, and shall allow a group of young people to apply with the support of a named adult.

requirements.text: The application process should be quick to complete for small grants.
requirements.quote: The application process should be quick to complete for small grants.

requirements.text: A grants officer can allocate applications to assessors, and two independent assessors are required for any application requesting more than 10,000.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to allocate applications to assessors, and the system shall require two independent assessors for any application requesting more than 10,000.

requirements.text: Assessors must declare any interest before seeing an application, and one who declares an interest cannot see or score it.
requirements.quote: Before an assessor can see an application, they shall declare whether they have any interest in the applicant organisation, and an assessor who declares an interest shall not be able to see or score the application.

requirements.text: Every declaration of interest, including no interest, is recorded with date and person.
requirements.quote: The system shall record every declaration of interest, including declarations of no interest, with the date and the person who made it.

requirements.text: External volunteer assessors see only applications allocated to them and cannot see bank details or other assessors' scores.
requirements.quote: External volunteer assessors shall only see the applications allocated to them and shall not see the organisation's bank details or the scores of other assessors.

requirements.text: Assessors score each criterion on the round's scale with a comment, and the system calculates the weighted total.
requirements.quote: An assessor shall score each criterion on a scale defined for the round and shall write a comment for each score, and the system shall calculate the weighted total.

requirements.text: The system flags for moderation applications where two assessors' weighted totals differ by more than 20% of the maximum score.
requirements.quote: Where the weighted totals given by two assessors differ by more than 20% of the maximum score, the system shall flag the application for moderation.

requirements.text: The moderated score and reason for change are recorded and the original assessor scores are kept.
requirements.quote: The moderated score and the reason for any change from the assessors' scores shall be recorded, and the assessors' original scores shall be kept.

requirements.text: A grants officer carries out and records due diligence on every application recommended for funding before it goes to the decision-maker, including accounts, governing document and, over 25,000, a credit check.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall carry out due diligence on every application recommended for funding before it goes to the decision-maker, recording the checks made and their outcome.

requirements.text: A grants officer can decide grants of up to 5,000 under delegated authority.
requirements.quote: A grants officer can decide on grants of up to 5,000 under delegated authority.

requirements.text: The programme's grant panel decides grants from 5,001 to 25,000.
requirements.quote: The programme's grant panel decides on grants from 5,001 to 25,000.

requirements.text: The Cabinet member for communities decides grants from 25,001 to 100,000.
requirements.quote: The Cabinet member for communities decides on grants from 25,001 to 100,000.

requirements.text: Cabinet decides grants over 100,000.
requirements.quote: Cabinet decides on grants over 100,000.

requirements.text: The system routes each recommended application to the decision-maker required by the scheme of delegation, based on total value over the whole term (all years for multi-year Strategic Partnerships grants).
requirements.quote: The system shall route each recommended application to the decision-maker required by the scheme of delegation, based on the total value of the grant over its whole term.

requirements.text: A panel member with an interest declares it before the panel meets and the system excludes them from the decision.
requirements.quote: A grant panel member who has an interest in an application shall declare it before the panel meets, and the system shall exclude them from the decision on that application.

requirements.text: Each decision is recorded as approved, approved with conditions or declined, with decision-maker, date, amount approved and reasons.
requirements.quote: The system shall record each decision as approved, approved with conditions, or declined, with the decision-maker, the date, the amount approved and the reasons.

requirements.text: Total approved in a round must not exceed the round's budget, and the decision-maker sees the remaining budget before each decision.
requirements.quote: The total approved in a round shall not exceed the round's budget, and the system shall show the decision-maker the remaining budget before each decision.

requirements.text: Every applicant is told the decision by email within five working days of the decision, and declined applicants receive the assessors' comments as feedback.
requirements.quote: Every applicant shall be told the decision on their application by email within five working days of the decision, and declined applicants shall be given the assessors' comments as feedback.

requirements.text: Decisions on grants over 25,000 are published on the council's website showing organisation, amount and purpose.
requirements.quote: Decisions on grants over 25,000 shall be published on the council's website, showing the organisation, the amount and the purpose.

requirements.text: Each ward member can see their remaining allocation and recommend a grant to an eligible organisation for a project in their ward.
requirements.quote: Each ward member shall be able to see their remaining allocation for the year and recommend a grant to an eligible organisation for a project in their ward.

requirements.text: A ward member cannot recommend a grant to an organisation in which they have a declared interest in the register of members' interests.
requirements.quote: A ward member shall not be able to recommend a grant to an organisation in which they have declared an interest in the council's register of members' interests.

requirements.text: A grants officer checks every Ward Member Grant recommendation and approves or rejects it; a rejection returns the amount to the member's allocation.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall check every Ward Member Grant recommendation for eligibility and shall approve or reject it, and a rejected recommendation shall return the amount to the member's allocation.

requirements.text: Ward Member Grants cannot be recommended in the six weeks before a local election.
requirements.quote: Ward Member Grants shall not be recommended in the six weeks before a local election.

requirements.text: On approval the system generates a grant agreement from the programme template including amount, purpose, conditions, payment schedule and monitoring requirements.
requirements.quote: When a grant is approved, the system shall generate a grant agreement from the template for the programme, including the amount, the purpose, any conditions set by the decision-maker, the payment schedule and the monitoring requirements.

requirements.text: The recipient signs electronically through the system, with two people connected with the organisation signing for grants over 5,000.
requirements.quote: The grant recipient shall sign the grant agreement electronically through the system, and the agreement shall be signed by two people connected with the organisation for grants over 5,000.

requirements.text: No payment is made until the agreement is signed by the recipient and countersigned by the council.
requirements.quote: No payment shall be made on a grant until the grant agreement has been signed by the recipient and countersigned by the council.

requirements.text: A grant offer lapses if the agreement is not signed in time, and the amount returns to the round's budget.
requirements.quote: An offer of a grant shall lapse if the agreement is not signed within a reasonable time, and the amount shall be returned to the round's budget.

requirements.text: Grants up to 10,000 are paid in a single payment after signing; grants over 10,000 are paid in instalments per the payment schedule.
requirements.quote: Grants up to 10,000 shall be paid in a single payment after the agreement is signed, and grants over 10,000 shall be paid in instalments set out in the payment schedule.

requirements.text: For Strategic Partnerships grants, instalments after the first are released only once the previous quarter's monitoring report has been accepted.
requirements.quote: For Strategic Partnerships grants, instalments after the first shall only be released once the previous quarter's monitoring report has been accepted.

requirements.text: When a payment is due and conditions are met, the system creates a payment request with grant reference, amount, cost centre and verified bank details.
requirements.quote: When a payment is due under the payment schedule and its conditions have been met, the system shall create a payment request containing the grant reference, the amount, the cost centre and the recipient's verified bank details.

requirements.text: A finance officer reviews and releases each payment request, and the officer who approved the grant cannot release its payment.
requirements.quote: A finance officer shall review each payment request and release it to the finance system, and the system shall prevent the officer who approved the grant from releasing its payment.

requirements.text: The system records payment date and finance system reference when Finance confirms payment.
requirements.quote: The system shall record the payment date and the finance system reference when Finance confirms that a payment has been made.

requirements.text: The system automatically stops a payment request if the recipient's registration shows removed, dissolved or insolvent.
requirements.quote: The system shall stop a payment request automatically if the recipient organisation's charity or company registration shows it as removed, dissolved or in insolvency.

requirements.text: A recipient can request a variation through the system, explaining what and why.
requirements.quote: A recipient shall be able to request a variation to their grant through the system, explaining what they want to change and why.

requirements.text: A variation changing the grant amount is decided by the decision-maker required for the new total.
requirements.quote: A variation that changes the amount of the grant shall be decided by the decision-maker who would be required for the new total amount.

requirements.text: A variation moving less than 10% of the grant between budget items without changing the total is decided by a grants officer.
requirements.quote: A variation that moves less than 10% of the grant between budget items, without changing the total, shall be decided by a grants officer.

requirements.text: Every variation is recorded against the agreement, and both the original signed agreement and the varied agreement are kept.
requirements.quote: Every variation shall be recorded against the grant agreement, and the system shall keep the agreement as originally signed as well as the agreement as varied.

requirements.text: Recipients of grants up to 5,000 submit a single end-of-grant report.
requirements.quote: Recipients of grants up to 5,000 submit a single end-of-grant report.

requirements.text: Recipients of grants from 5,001 to 25,000 submit a mid-point report and an end-of-grant report.
requirements.quote: Recipients of grants from 5,001 to 25,000 submit a mid-point report and an end-of-grant report.

requirements.text: Recipients of grants over 25,000 submit quarterly reports and an end-of-grant report with evidence of expenditure.
requirements.quote: Recipients of grants over 25,000 submit quarterly reports and an end-of-grant report with evidence of expenditure.

requirements.text: The system reminds recipients 14 days before a report is due and on the due date, and marks it overdue if not submitted within 14 days after the due date.
requirements.quote: The system shall remind the recipient of each monitoring report 14 days before it is due and again on the due date, and shall mark the report as overdue if it is not submitted within 14 days after the due date.

requirements.text: A grants officer reviews each monitoring report, records whether it is accepted, and may ask for more information.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall review each monitoring report and record whether it is accepted, and may ask the recipient for more information.

requirements.text: Monitoring reports collect the outcome measures set for the round.
requirements.quote: Monitoring reports shall collect the outcome measures set for the round, so that the council can report the outcomes achieved across all grants in a programme.

requirements.text: A grants officer can start a clawback, recording amount and reason, and the system sends a repayment request to the recipient.
requirements.quote: Where a grant has not been used for its agreed purpose, a grants officer shall be able to start a clawback, recording the amount to be recovered and the reason, and the system shall send a request for repayment to the recipient.

requirements.text: A clawback over 5,000 must be approved by the programme manager before the repayment request is sent.
requirements.quote: A clawback over 5,000 shall be approved by the programme manager before the request for repayment is sent.

requirements.text: A grant is closed when the end-of-grant report is accepted and every payment and any clawback is completed.
requirements.quote: A grant shall be closed when the end-of-grant report has been accepted and every payment and any clawback has been completed.

requirements.text: The system reports grants awarded and paid for any period by programme, round, ward and organisation.
requirements.quote: The system shall report, for any period, the grants awarded and paid by programme, round, ward and organisation.

requirements.text: The system shows, for any organisation, every application and every grant received across all programmes.
requirements.quote: The system shall show, for any organisation, every application it has made and every grant it has received from the council across all programmes.

requirements.text: The system reports applications received, approved and declined per round, with decline reasons, by ward and by equality information.
requirements.quote: The system shall report the applications received, approved and declined in each round, with the reasons for declining, by ward and by the equality information applicants provided.

requirements.text: Each ward member can see grants awarded in their ward under all programmes.
requirements.quote: Each ward member shall be able to see the grants awarded in their ward under all programmes.

requirements.text: Auditors have read-only access to every record, including declarations of interest, decisions, and bank detail changes and verification.
requirements.quote: Auditors shall be able to see every record in the system, including declarations of interest, decisions, bank detail changes and their verification, without being able to change anything.

requirements.text: The applicant-facing parts meet WCAG 2.2 AA and work on mobile phones as well as computers.
requirements.quote: The applicant-facing parts of the system shall meet the WCAG 2.2 AA standard and shall work on mobile phones as well as on computers.

requirements.text: A first-time applicant with documents to hand can complete an application for a grant under 1,000 in no more than 30 minutes.
requirements.quote: The application process for a grant under 1,000 shall be completable in no more than 30 minutes by a first-time applicant who has their organisation documents to hand.

requirements.text: The system is available at least 99.5% of the time, with no planned maintenance in the last 48 hours before a round closes.
requirements.quote: The system shall be available at least 99.5% of the time, and in the last 48 hours before a round closes it shall have no planned maintenance.

requirements.text: The system supports at least 500 concurrent applicants without any page taking more than three seconds to load.
requirements.quote: The system shall support at least 500 applicants working on applications at the same time without a page taking more than three seconds to load.

requirements.text: Council users sign in with single sign-on; applicants and external assessors use email, password and a second factor.
requirements.quote: Council users shall sign in with the council's single sign-on, and applicants and external assessors shall sign in with an email address, a password and a second factor.

requirements.text: A grants officer can remove service users' personal data included by mistake without deleting the rest of the application.
requirements.quote: Personal data about applicants' service users, if any is included in an application by mistake, shall be removable by a grants officer without deleting the rest of the application.

requirements.text: Approved grant records are kept seven years after closure and declined application records two years after decision, then deleted.
requirements.quote: The system shall retain records of approved grants for seven years after the grant is closed and records of declined applications for two years after the decision, and shall then delete them.

requirements.text: Equality information is optional, kept separately from the application, and not visible to assessors or decision-makers.
requirements.quote: Equality information given by applicants shall be optional, shall be kept separately from the application, and shall not be visible to assessors or decision-makers.

requirements.text: Every change to a record is audited with user, date/time and before and after values, and the audit record cannot be edited or deleted by any user.
requirements.quote: Every action that changes a record in the system shall be recorded with the user, the date and time, and the value before and after the change, and the audit record shall not be editable or deletable by any user.

requirements.text: Grants from the three financial years before go-live are migrated with organisation, amount, programme and status.
requirements.quote: Grants made in the three financial years before go-live shall be migrated into the system with their organisation, amount, programme and status, so that reports of funding to an organisation are complete.

requirements.text: Organisation records that appear to be duplicates are presented to a grants officer to decide whether to merge before migration.
requirements.quote: Before migration, organisation records that appear to refer to the same organisation shall be presented to a grants officer for a decision on whether to merge them.

requirements.text: In-progress Strategic Partnerships grants are migrated with agreements, payment schedules and monitoring reports.
requirements.quote: Strategic Partnerships grants that are in progress at go-live shall be migrated with their agreements, payment schedules and monitoring reports, so that they can be managed in the system from go-live.

requirements.text: The system must let each programme's own rules be applied without affecting other programmes.
requirements.quote: The system must allow these rules to be applied for the programme concerned without affecting other programmes.

requirements.text: A Neighbourhood Fund application records the neighbourhood served, and the system adds the round's priority weighting to the weighted score for priority neighbourhoods.
requirements.quote: A Neighbourhood Fund application shall record the neighbourhood the project serves, chosen from the council's list of neighbourhoods, and the system shall add the priority weighting set for the round to the weighted score of applications from priority neighbourhoods.

requirements.text: An organisation cannot receive more than one Neighbourhood Fund grant in a financial year.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall not receive more than one Neighbourhood Fund grant in the same financial year.

requirements.text: Strategic Partnerships agreements state that years two and three are subject to the council's annual budget, and the programme manager must confirm each year's funding before its first instalment is released.
requirements.quote: A Strategic Partnerships grant agreement shall state that the second and third years' funding is subject to the council's annual budget, and the system shall require the programme manager to confirm each year's funding before its first instalment is released.

requirements.text: Each Strategic Partnerships grant has a named relationship manager and a note of each quarterly meeting is recorded against the grant.
requirements.quote: Each Strategic Partnerships grant shall have a named relationship manager, and the system shall record a note of each quarterly meeting against the grant.

requirements.text: For Small Sparks grants paid via a sponsor, the system records the sponsor, verifies its bank details as for a recipient, and requires the sponsor to sign the agreement as well as the group.
requirements.quote: Where a Small Sparks grant is paid through a sponsoring organisation, the system shall record the sponsor, verify the sponsor's bank details in the same way as a recipient's, and require the sponsor to sign the grant agreement as well as the group.

requirements.text: A Small Sparks decision is made within ten working days of submission, and the programme manager is alerted to any application undecided after eight working days.
requirements.quote: A decision on a Small Sparks application shall be made within ten working days of submission, and the system shall alert the programme manager about any application still undecided after eight working days.

requirements.text: Youth Voice assessors may be youth council members aged 16 or over, and the system records that an assessor is a youth panel member and the supporting youth worker's name.
requirements.quote: Assessors for the Youth Voice fund may be members of the youth council aged 16 or over, and the system shall record that an assessor is a youth panel member and the name of the supporting youth worker.

requirements.text: An Arts in the Open grant is not paid until the event permission is uploaded, and the system records the permission reference.
requirements.quote: An Arts in the Open grant shall not be paid until the applicant has uploaded the event permission from the council's events team, and the system shall record the permission reference.

requirements.text: If an Arts in the Open event is cancelled for bad weather, the recipient keeps costs incurred and a grants officer can record a partial clawback of the remainder.
requirements.quote: If an Arts in the Open event is cancelled because of bad weather, the recipient may keep costs already incurred, and the system shall allow a grants officer to record a partial clawback of the remainder.

requirements.text: Winter Warmth grants are approved only for activities between 1 November and 31 March, and the end-of-grant report is due by 30 April.
requirements.quote: Winter Warmth grants shall only be approved for activities that take place between 1 November and 31 March, and the end-of-grant report shall be due by 30 April.

questions.text: Who may extend a deadline for an individual applicant, a grants officer or only the programme manager? Does an extension override the rule that applications cannot be submitted after closing? Are extensions limited to technical problems?
questions.quote: Grants officers sometimes extend the deadline for an individual applicant who had technical problems.

questions.text: How must the system establish that the two people connected with an organisation are 'not related to each other' (self-declaration, evidence, a check)? What counts as related?
questions.quote: the details of at least two people connected with it who are not related to each other.

questions.text: What is the income threshold below which accounts need not be provided, and what must new groups with no accounts provide in the meantime? Until it is set, is the accounts document mandatory for all organisations?
questions.quote: Programme managers have suggested that small organisations with an annual income below a threshold should not have to provide accounts, but the threshold has not been set.

questions.text: What measurable standard applies to 'quick to complete' for small grants? The only figure given is 30 minutes for grants under 1,000. Does it apply to other small grants, and is this a requirement or an aspiration given the word 'should'?
questions.quote: The application process should be quick to complete for small grants.

questions.text: What is the Small Sparks grant range? Section 1.1 says up to 1,000, while Appendix A says 100 to 1,500. Which applies to the single-assessor, usability (under 1,000) and other thresholds?
questions.quote: Small Sparks grants range from 100 to 1,500

questions.text: What is the time limit after which a grant offer lapses? 'A reasonable time' cannot be configured or tested, and Legal Services advice is pending. Must the system support different periods by programme or amount?
questions.quote: An offer of a grant shall lapse if the agreement is not signed within a reasonable time, and the amount shall be returned to the round's budget.

questions.text: What is the 10% measured against (whole-term grant, the year's grant, or a budget line)? Who decides variations that move 10% or more without changing the total, and variations to time or project scale, which section 11 describes as possible but gives no decision-maker?
questions.quote: A variation that moves less than 10% of the grant between budget items, without changing the total, shall be decided by a grants officer.

questions.text: How and how often does the system learn of a change in a registration's status (removed, dissolved, insolvent)? Is it a live check at each payment request, a periodic check, or manual?
questions.quote: The system shall stop a payment request automatically if the recipient organisation's charity or company registration shows it as removed, dissolved or in insolvency.

questions.text: How are conditions attached to an approved grant (for example, landowner consent) recorded and marked as met, and who confirms this, so the system knows a payment's conditions have been met?
questions.quote: When a payment is due under the payment schedule and its conditions have been met

questions.text: How does the retention and deletion rule reconcile with the rule that audit records cannot be deleted by any user, and with the audit trail holding before and after values, including personal data removed under the service-user data rule? Who or what performs the deletion?
questions.quote: The system shall retain records of approved grants for seven years after the grant is closed and records of declined applications for two years after the decision, and shall then delete them.

questions.text: Can Youth Voice panel members under 18 take part in decisions recorded in the system, or must an adult record them? Appendix A says assessors must be 16 or over; what is the rule for panel members under 16, and who records decisions?
questions.quote: The Youth Voice fund panel includes young people who are under 18. Legal Services are considering whether they can take part in decisions recorded in the system or whether an adult must record the decision for them.

questions.text: Is the system to notify ward members when an organisation in their ward applies to any programme? This is undecided, so it is not known whether it is in scope.
questions.quote: Some ward members have asked to be told when an organisation in their ward applies to any programme; no decision has been made.

questions.text: What other checks make up due diligence beyond accounts, governing document and credit check? Does the full set apply to every programme, including small and quick grants such as Small Sparks and Ward Member Grants?
questions.quote: Due diligence includes checking the organisation's accounts, its governing document and, for grants over 25,000, a credit check.

questions.text: Which programmes fund individuals, and how are individuals (as opposed to organisations or youth groups) registered and identified, given that registration and the applicant record are built around organisations?
questions.quote: and, in a small number of programmes, individuals.

questions.text: How is the 'date by which a decision is expected' determined for the acknowledgement email (per round, per programme, a fixed period)? The document does not say where it is set.
questions.quote: When an application is submitted the system shall send the applicant an acknowledgement by email with a reference number and the date by which a decision is expected.

questions.text: Which period is the 99.5% availability measured over (monthly, annually), and are planned maintenance windows excluded from the calculation?
questions.quote: The system shall be available at least 99.5% of the time

questions.text: What happens at go-live to in-progress grants from programmes other than Strategic Partnerships? Only organisation, amount, programme and status are migrated for them, so how will their payment schedules, agreements and monitoring be managed in the system?
questions.quote: Grants made in the three financial years before go-live shall be migrated into the system with their organisation, amount, programme and status, so that reports of funding to an organisation are complete.

requirements.text: A grants officer can create a round for a programme, recording its opening and closing date and time, budget, minimum and maximum grant, eligibility questions, application questions and weighted assessment criteria.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to create a round for a programme, recording its opening and closing date and time, its budget, the minimum and maximum grant that can be requested, the eligibility questions, the application questions and the assessment criteria with their weightings.

requirements.text: A round can only be opened once its programme manager has approved its set-up, and the system records who approved it and when.
requirements.quote: A round shall only be opened once its programme manager has approved its set-up, and the system shall record who approved it and when.

requirements.text: The total budget of the rounds in a programme in a financial year must not exceed the programme's budget for that year.
requirements.quote: The system shall not allow the budget of the rounds in a programme in one financial year to exceed the programme's budget for that year.

requirements.text: A grants officer can copy a previous round as the starting point for a new one.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to copy a previous round as the starting point for a new one.

requirements.text: A round can be open to all eligible applicants or by invitation only; in an invitation-only round only invited organisations can start an application.
requirements.quote: A round may be open to all eligible applicants or by invitation only; for an invitation-only round, the system shall only let invited organisations start an application.

requirements.text: No applications are accepted after the round's closing date and time, and an application still being completed at closing cannot be submitted.
requirements.quote: Applications shall not be accepted after a round's closing date and time, and an application that is being completed when the round closes shall not be submittable.

requirements.text: The programme manager can extend the closing date for a single applicant, recording the reason, and the extension shows in the round's audit history.
requirements.quote: The programme manager shall be able to extend the closing date for a single applicant, recording the reason, and the extension shall be shown in the round's audit history.

requirements.text: A person can register an organisation by giving its name, address, legal form, charity or company number if it has one, and details of at least two unrelated people connected with it.
requirements.quote: A person shall be able to register an organisation in the system by giving its name, address, legal form, charity or company number if it has one, and the details of at least two people connected with it who are not related to each other.

requirements.text: Where a charity or company number is given, the system checks it against the public register and shows the officer any differences in registered name and address.
requirements.quote: Where a charity or company number is given, the system shall check it against the public register and shall show the officer any difference between the registered name and address and those entered.

requirements.text: The system prevents registration of an organisation whose charity or company number is already held on another record and directs the person to request access to the existing record.
requirements.quote: The system shall prevent the registration of an organisation whose charity or company number is already held on another organisation record, and shall direct the person to request access to the existing record.

requirements.text: An organisation record can have several users, and existing users approve any request from a new user to join.
requirements.quote: An organisation record shall be able to have several users, and the organisation's existing users shall approve any request by a new user to join it.

requirements.text: If no remaining user can approve a request, a grants officer can add a user after verifying the person's connection with the organisation.
requirements.quote: If an organisation has no remaining users who can approve a request, a grants officer shall be able to add a user after verifying the person's connection with the organisation.

requirements.text: An organisation can upload its governing document, latest accounts, safeguarding policy and equality policy once, and the system attaches the current versions to each application automatically.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall be able to upload its governing document, latest accounts, safeguarding policy and equality policy to its organisation record once, and the system shall attach the current versions to each application automatically.

requirements.text: The system records an expiry date for each organisation document and asks the organisation to upload a new version when one expires.
requirements.quote: The system shall record an expiry date for each organisation document and shall ask the organisation to upload a new version when one expires.

requirements.text: Accounts are treated as expired 18 months after the end of the financial year they cover.
requirements.quote: Accounts shall be treated as expired 18 months after the end of the financial year they cover.

requirements.text: An organisation enters its bank details, and the system verifies the account name matches the organisation's name using the council's bank account verification service before the details can be used for a payment.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall enter its bank details in the system, and the system shall verify that the account name matches the organisation's name using the council's bank account verification service before the details can be used for a payment.

requirements.text: A change to bank details only takes effect after a grants officer confirms it by telephone, using a number already on the record, and the system records who called and when.
requirements.quote: A change to an organisation's bank details shall only take effect after a grants officer has confirmed it by telephone with a person connected with the organisation, using a telephone number already held on the record, and the system shall record who made the call and when.

requirements.text: No payment is released to bank details changed in the previous 10 working days until a finance officer has reviewed the change.
requirements.quote: No payment shall be released to bank details that were changed in the previous 10 working days until a finance officer has reviewed the change.

requirements.text: Before starting an application the applicant answers the round's eligibility questions, and the system immediately says whether they are eligible and, if not, which answer made them ineligible.
requirements.quote: Before starting an application, an applicant shall answer the round's eligibility questions, and the system shall tell them immediately whether they are eligible, and if not, which answer made them ineligible.

requirements.text: An ineligible applicant is shown the contact details of the grants team and of the local umbrella body.
requirements.quote: An applicant who is not eligible shall be shown the contact details of the grants team and of the local umbrella body that can offer advice.

requirements.text: The system prevents an organisation applying to a round if it has an overdue monitoring report on any previous grant.
requirements.quote: The system shall prevent an organisation from applying to a round if it has an overdue monitoring report on any previous grant.

requirements.text: An organisation cannot hold more than one open application to the same round.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall not hold more than one open application to the same round.

requirements.text: The application form saves answers automatically, and the applicant can leave and return at any time before the round closes.
requirements.quote: The application form shall save the applicant's answers automatically as they are entered, and the applicant shall be able to leave and return to the application at any time before the round closes.

requirements.text: Several users of an organisation can work on an application but only one can edit at a time, and the system shows who is editing.
requirements.quote: Several users of the same organisation shall be able to work on an application, but only one shall be able to edit it at a time, and the system shall show who is editing.

requirements.text: The application includes a budget table listing each item, its cost and whether capital or revenue, and the system calculates the total and checks it equals the amount requested.
requirements.quote: The application shall include a budget table in which the applicant lists each item of expenditure, its cost and whether it is capital or revenue, and the system shall calculate the total and check that it equals the amount requested.

requirements.text: The system does not allow a request below the round's minimum or above its maximum grant.
requirements.quote: The system shall not allow an application to request less than the round's minimum or more than its maximum grant.

requirements.text: Before submitting, the applicant confirms a declaration that the information is true, and the system records who confirmed it and when.
requirements.quote: Before submitting, the applicant shall confirm a declaration that the information given is true, and the system shall record the name of the person who confirmed it and the date and time.

requirements.text: On submission the system emails the applicant an acknowledgement with a reference number and the date a decision is expected.
requirements.quote: When an application is submitted the system shall send the applicant an acknowledgement by email with a reference number and the date by which a decision is expected.

requirements.text: A grants officer can complete and submit an application for an applicant who cannot apply online, recording that they did so and the applicant's confirmation of the declaration.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to complete and submit an application on behalf of an applicant who cannot apply online, recording that they did so and the applicant's confirmation of the declaration.

requirements.text: The Youth Voice application form uses plain language suitable for ages 13 to 25 and lets a group of young people apply with a named adult's support.
requirements.quote: The Youth Voice fund application form shall use plain language suitable for applicants aged 13 to 25, and shall allow a group of young people to apply with the support of a named adult.

requirements.text: The application process should be quick to complete for small grants.
requirements.quote: The application process should be quick to complete for small grants.

requirements.text: A grants officer can allocate applications to assessors, and the system requires two independent assessors for any application requesting more than 10,000.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall be able to allocate applications to assessors, and the system shall require two independent assessors for any application requesting more than 10,000.

requirements.text: Assessors must declare any interest in the applicant before seeing an application, and an assessor who declares an interest cannot see or score it.
requirements.quote: Before an assessor can see an application, they shall declare whether they have any interest in the applicant organisation, and an assessor who declares an interest shall not be able to see or score the application.

requirements.text: The system records every declaration of interest, including declarations of no interest, with date and person.
requirements.quote: The system shall record every declaration of interest, including declarations of no interest, with the date and the person who made it.

requirements.text: External volunteer assessors see only applications allocated to them and cannot see bank details or other assessors' scores.
requirements.quote: External volunteer assessors shall only see the applications allocated to them and shall not see the organisation's bank details or the scores of other assessors.

requirements.text: An assessor scores each criterion on the round's scale with a comment for each score, and the system calculates the weighted total.
requirements.quote: An assessor shall score each criterion on a scale defined for the round and shall write a comment for each score, and the system shall calculate the weighted total.

requirements.text: The system flags an application for moderation where two assessors' weighted totals differ by more than 20% of the maximum score.
requirements.quote: Where the weighted totals given by two assessors differ by more than 20% of the maximum score, the system shall flag the application for moderation.

requirements.text: The moderated score and reason for any change are recorded, and the assessors' original scores are kept.
requirements.quote: The moderated score and the reason for any change from the assessors' scores shall be recorded, and the assessors' original scores shall be kept.

requirements.text: A grants officer carries out and records due diligence on every application recommended for funding before it goes to the decision-maker, including checks of accounts, governing document and, over 25,000, a credit check.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall carry out due diligence on every application recommended for funding before it goes to the decision-maker, recording the checks made and their outcome.

requirements.text: The system routes each recommended application to the decision-maker required by the scheme of delegation, based on the total value over the grant's whole term.
requirements.quote: The system shall route each recommended application to the decision-maker required by the scheme of delegation, based on the total value of the grant over its whole term.

requirements.text: A grant panel member with an interest must declare it before the panel meets, and the system excludes them from the decision.
requirements.quote: A grant panel member who has an interest in an application shall declare it before the panel meets, and the system shall exclude them from the decision on that application.

requirements.text: The system records each decision as approved, approved with conditions or declined, with decision-maker, date, amount and reasons.
requirements.quote: The system shall record each decision as approved, approved with conditions, or declined, with the decision-maker, the date, the amount approved and the reasons.

requirements.text: Total approved in a round must not exceed the round's budget, and the decision-maker is shown the remaining budget before each decision.
requirements.quote: The total approved in a round shall not exceed the round's budget, and the system shall show the decision-maker the remaining budget before each decision.

requirements.text: Every applicant is told the decision by email within five working days, and declined applicants receive the assessors' comments as feedback.
requirements.quote: Every applicant shall be told the decision on their application by email within five working days of the decision, and declined applicants shall be given the assessors' comments as feedback.

requirements.text: Decisions on grants over 25,000 are published on the council's website showing organisation, amount and purpose.
requirements.quote: Decisions on grants over 25,000 shall be published on the council's website, showing the organisation, the amount and the purpose.

requirements.text: Each ward member can see their remaining allocation and recommend a grant to an eligible organisation for a project in their ward.
requirements.quote: Each ward member shall be able to see their remaining allocation for the year and recommend a grant to an eligible organisation for a project in their ward.

requirements.text: A ward member cannot recommend a grant to an organisation in which they have a declared interest in the register of members' interests.
requirements.quote: A ward member shall not be able to recommend a grant to an organisation in which they have declared an interest in the council's register of members' interests.

requirements.text: A grants officer checks every Ward Member Grant recommendation and approves or rejects it; a rejected one returns the amount to the member's allocation.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall check every Ward Member Grant recommendation for eligibility and shall approve or reject it, and a rejected recommendation shall return the amount to the member's allocation.

requirements.text: Ward Member Grants cannot be recommended in the six weeks before a local election.
requirements.quote: Ward Member Grants shall not be recommended in the six weeks before a local election.

requirements.text: On approval the system generates a grant agreement from the programme template including amount, purpose, conditions, payment schedule and monitoring requirements.
requirements.quote: When a grant is approved, the system shall generate a grant agreement from the template for the programme, including the amount, the purpose, any conditions set by the decision-maker, the payment schedule and the monitoring requirements.

requirements.text: The recipient signs the agreement electronically, and for grants over 5,000 two people connected with the organisation must sign.
requirements.quote: The grant recipient shall sign the grant agreement electronically through the system, and the agreement shall be signed by two people connected with the organisation for grants over 5,000.

requirements.text: No payment is made until the agreement has been signed by the recipient and countersigned by the council.
requirements.quote: No payment shall be made on a grant until the grant agreement has been signed by the recipient and countersigned by the council.

requirements.text: A grant offer lapses if the agreement is not signed in time, and the amount returns to the round's budget.
requirements.quote: An offer of a grant shall lapse if the agreement is not signed within a reasonable time, and the amount shall be returned to the round's budget.

requirements.text: Grants up to 10,000 are paid in a single payment after signing; grants over 10,000 are paid in instalments per the payment schedule.
requirements.quote: Grants up to 10,000 shall be paid in a single payment after the agreement is signed, and grants over 10,000 shall be paid in instalments set out in the payment schedule.

requirements.text: For Strategic Partnerships grants, instalments after the first are released only once the previous quarter's monitoring report has been accepted.
requirements.quote: For Strategic Partnerships grants, instalments after the first shall only be released once the previous quarter's monitoring report has been accepted.

requirements.text: When a payment is due and its conditions are met, the system creates a payment request with grant reference, amount, cost centre and verified bank details.
requirements.quote: When a payment is due under the payment schedule and its conditions have been met, the system shall create a payment request containing the grant reference, the amount, the cost centre and the recipient's verified bank details.

requirements.text: A finance officer reviews and releases each payment request, and the officer who approved the grant cannot release its payment.
requirements.quote: A finance officer shall review each payment request and release it to the finance system, and the system shall prevent the officer who approved the grant from releasing its payment.

requirements.text: The system records the payment date and finance system reference when Finance confirms payment.
requirements.quote: The system shall record the payment date and the finance system reference when Finance confirms that a payment has been made.

requirements.text: The system automatically stops a payment request if the recipient's registration shows it as removed, dissolved or in insolvency.
requirements.quote: The system shall stop a payment request automatically if the recipient organisation's charity or company registration shows it as removed, dissolved or in insolvency.

requirements.text: A recipient can request a variation through the system, explaining what and why.
requirements.quote: A recipient shall be able to request a variation to their grant through the system, explaining what they want to change and why.

requirements.text: A variation changing the grant amount is decided by the decision-maker required for the new total.
requirements.quote: A variation that changes the amount of the grant shall be decided by the decision-maker who would be required for the new total amount.

requirements.text: A variation moving less than 10% of the grant between budget items without changing the total is decided by a grants officer.
requirements.quote: A variation that moves less than 10% of the grant between budget items, without changing the total, shall be decided by a grants officer.

requirements.text: Every variation is recorded against the agreement, and both the original signed agreement and the varied agreement are kept.
requirements.quote: Every variation shall be recorded against the grant agreement, and the system shall keep the agreement as originally signed as well as the agreement as varied.

requirements.text: Recipients of grants up to 5,000 submit a single end-of-grant report.
requirements.quote: Recipients of grants up to 5,000 submit a single end-of-grant report.

requirements.text: Recipients of grants from 5,001 to 25,000 submit a mid-point report and an end-of-grant report.
requirements.quote: Recipients of grants from 5,001 to 25,000 submit a mid-point report and an end-of-grant report.

requirements.text: Recipients of grants over 25,000 submit quarterly reports and an end-of-grant report with evidence of expenditure.
requirements.quote: Recipients of grants over 25,000 submit quarterly reports and an end-of-grant report with evidence of expenditure.

requirements.text: The system reminds the recipient 14 days before a report is due and on the due date, and marks it overdue if not submitted within 14 days after the due date.
requirements.quote: The system shall remind the recipient of each monitoring report 14 days before it is due and again on the due date, and shall mark the report as overdue if it is not submitted within 14 days after the due date.

requirements.text: A grants officer reviews each monitoring report, records whether it is accepted, and may ask for more information.
requirements.quote: A grants officer shall review each monitoring report and record whether it is accepted, and may ask the recipient for more information.

requirements.text: Monitoring reports collect the outcome measures set for the round.
requirements.quote: Monitoring reports shall collect the outcome measures set for the round, so that the council can report the outcomes achieved across all grants in a programme.

requirements.text: A grants officer can start a clawback, recording amount and reason, and the system sends a repayment request to the recipient.
requirements.quote: Where a grant has not been used for its agreed purpose, a grants officer shall be able to start a clawback, recording the amount to be recovered and the reason, and the system shall send a request for repayment to the recipient.

requirements.text: A clawback over 5,000 must be approved by the programme manager before the repayment request is sent.
requirements.quote: A clawback over 5,000 shall be approved by the programme manager before the request for repayment is sent.

requirements.text: A grant is closed when the end-of-grant report is accepted and every payment and any clawback is completed.
requirements.quote: A grant shall be closed when the end-of-grant report has been accepted and every payment and any clawback has been completed.

requirements.text: The system reports grants awarded and paid by programme, round, ward and organisation for any period.
requirements.quote: The system shall report, for any period, the grants awarded and paid by programme, round, ward and organisation.

requirements.text: The system shows, for any organisation, every application made and every grant received across all programmes.
requirements.quote: The system shall show, for any organisation, every application it has made and every grant it has received from the council across all programmes.

requirements.text: The system reports applications received, approved and declined per round, with decline reasons, by ward and by equality information.
requirements.quote: The system shall report the applications received, approved and declined in each round, with the reasons for declining, by ward and by the equality information applicants provided.

requirements.text: Each ward member can see grants awarded in their ward under all programmes.
requirements.quote: Each ward member shall be able to see the grants awarded in their ward under all programmes.

requirements.text: Auditors can see every record, including declarations of interest, decisions, bank detail changes and verification, read-only.
requirements.quote: Auditors shall be able to see every record in the system, including declarations of interest, decisions, bank detail changes and their verification, without being able to change anything.

requirements.text: Applicant-facing parts meet WCAG 2.2 AA and work on mobile phones and computers.
requirements.quote: The applicant-facing parts of the system shall meet the WCAG 2.2 AA standard and shall work on mobile phones as well as on computers.

requirements.text: A first-time applicant with documents to hand can complete an application for a grant under 1,000 in no more than 30 minutes.
requirements.quote: The application process for a grant under 1,000 shall be completable in no more than 30 minutes by a first-time applicant who has their organisation documents to hand.

requirements.text: The system is available at least 99.5% of the time and has no planned maintenance in the last 48 hours before a round closes.
requirements.quote: The system shall be available at least 99.5% of the time, and in the last 48 hours before a round closes it shall have no planned maintenance.

requirements.text: The system supports at least 500 concurrent applicants without any page taking more than three seconds to load.
requirements.quote: The system shall support at least 500 applicants working on applications at the same time without a page taking more than three seconds to load.

requirements.text: Council users sign in with single sign-on; applicants and external assessors sign in with email, password and a second factor.
requirements.quote: Council users shall sign in with the council's single sign-on, and applicants and external assessors shall sign in with an email address, a password and a second factor.

requirements.text: A grants officer can remove personal data about service users mistakenly included in an application without deleting the rest of the application.
requirements.quote: Personal data about applicants' service users, if any is included in an application by mistake, shall be removable by a grants officer without deleting the rest of the application.

requirements.text: Records of approved grants are kept seven years after closure and declined applications two years after decision, then deleted.
requirements.quote: The system shall retain records of approved grants for seven years after the grant is closed and records of declined applications for two years after the decision, and shall then delete them.

requirements.text: Equality information is optional, kept separate from the application, and not visible to assessors or decision-makers.
requirements.quote: Equality information given by applicants shall be optional, shall be kept separately from the application, and shall not be visible to assessors or decision-makers.

requirements.text: Every change to a record is logged with user, date and time and before and after values, and the audit record cannot be edited or deleted by any user.
requirements.quote: Every action that changes a record in the system shall be recorded with the user, the date and time, and the value before and after the change, and the audit record shall not be editable or deletable by any user.

requirements.text: Grants from the three financial years before go-live are migrated with organisation, amount, programme and status.
requirements.quote: Grants made in the three financial years before go-live shall be migrated into the system with their organisation, amount, programme and status, so that reports of funding to an organisation are complete.

requirements.text: Organisation records that appear to be the same organisation are presented to a grants officer to decide whether to merge before migration.
requirements.quote: Before migration, organisation records that appear to refer to the same organisation shall be presented to a grants officer for a decision on whether to merge them.

requirements.text: In-progress Strategic Partnerships grants are migrated with agreements, payment schedules and monitoring reports.
requirements.quote: Strategic Partnerships grants that are in progress at go-live shall be migrated with their agreements, payment schedules and monitoring reports, so that they can be managed in the system from go-live.

requirements.text: The system must allow each programme's own rules to be applied without affecting other programmes.
requirements.quote: The system must allow these rules to be applied for the programme concerned without affecting other programmes.

requirements.text: Neighbourhood Fund applications record the neighbourhood served from the council's list, and the system adds the round's priority weighting to scores of applications from priority neighbourhoods.
requirements.quote: A Neighbourhood Fund application shall record the neighbourhood the project serves, chosen from the council's list of neighbourhoods, and the system shall add the priority weighting set for the round to the weighted score of applications from priority neighbourhoods.

requirements.text: An organisation cannot receive more than one Neighbourhood Fund grant in the same financial year.
requirements.quote: An organisation shall not receive more than one Neighbourhood Fund grant in the same financial year.

requirements.text: Strategic Partnerships agreements state years two and three are subject to the council's annual budget, and the programme manager must confirm each year's funding before its first instalment is released.
requirements.quote: A Strategic Partnerships grant agreement shall state that the second and third years' funding is subject to the council's annual budget, and the system shall require the programme manager to confirm each year's funding before its first instalment is released.

requirements.text: Each Strategic Partnerships grant has a named relationship manager, and a note of each quarterly meeting is recorded against the grant.
requirements.quote: Each Strategic Partnerships grant shall have a named relationship manager, and the system shall record a note of each quarterly meeting against the grant.

requirements.text: Where a Small Sparks grant is paid through a sponsor, the system records the sponsor, verifies its bank details as for a recipient, and requires the sponsor to sign the agreement as well as the group.
requirements.quote: Where a Small Sparks grant is paid through a sponsoring organisation, the system shall record the sponsor, verify the sponsor's bank details in the same way as a recipient's, and require the sponsor to sign the grant agreement as well as the group.

requirements.text: A Small Sparks decision is made within ten working days of submission, and the programme manager is alerted about any application undecided after eight working days.
requirements.quote: A decision on a Small Sparks application shall be made within ten working days of submission, and the system shall alert the programme manager about any application still undecided after eight working days.

requirements.text: Youth Voice assessors may be youth council members aged 16 or over, and the system records that an assessor is a youth panel member and the supporting youth worker's name.
requirements.quote: Assessors for the Youth Voice fund may be members of the youth council aged 16 or over, and the system shall record that an assessor is a youth panel member and the name of the supporting youth worker.

requirements.text: An Arts in the Open grant is not paid until the event permission from the events team is uploaded, and the permission reference is recorded.
requirements.quote: An Arts in the Open grant shall not be paid until the applicant has uploaded the event permission from the council's events team, and the system shall record the permission reference.

requirements.text: If an Arts in the Open event is cancelled for bad weather, the system lets a grants officer record a partial clawback of the remainder.
requirements.quote: If an Arts in the Open event is cancelled because of bad weather, the recipient may keep costs already incurred, and the system shall allow a grants officer to record a partial clawback of the remainder.

requirements.text: Winter Warmth grants are only approved for activities between 1 November and 31 March, and the end-of-grant report is due by 30 April.
requirements.quote: Winter Warmth grants shall only be approved for activities that take place between 1 November and 31 March, and the end-of-grant report shall be due by 30 April.

questions.text: Closing dates cannot be passed, yet extensions for individual applicants are allowed. The text says grants officers sometimes extend deadlines, but the requirement gives the power only to the programme manager. Who may grant an extension, is there a limit on its length, and how does it sit with the rule that no application is accepted after closing?
questions.quote: Applications shall not be accepted after a round's closing date and time, and an application that is being completed when the round closes shall not be submittable. Grants officers sometimes extend the deadline for an individual applicant who had technical problems.

questions.text: What period counts as 'a reasonable time' for signing a grant agreement before an offer lapses? Section 16.2 says Legal Services have not yet advised. Is it a fixed period, configurable per programme, and are reminders needed before lapse?
questions.quote: An offer of a grant shall lapse if the agreement is not signed within a reasonable time, and the amount shall be returned to the round's budget.

questions.text: Small Sparks is described as grants 'up to 1,000' in section 1.1 but as ranging from 100 to 1,500 in Appendix A. Which is correct? This also decides which grants the 30-minute completion requirement (grants under 1,000) covers, and which grants count as 'small grants' for the usability and single-assessor rules.
questions.quote: Small Sparks grants range from 100 to 1,500, and groups without a bank account in their own name may be paid through a sponsoring organisation.

questions.text: What is the 10% in the variation rule measured against: the whole grant over its term, the current year's grant, or the budget line moved from? The worked example uses 'the year's grant' for a multi-year grant, and the choice changes who decides the variation. Is the 10% limit also cumulative across several variations on one grant?
questions.quote: A variation that moves less than 10% of the grant between budget items, without changing the total, shall be decided by a grants officer.

questions.text: Who decides variations that neither change the amount nor move under 10% between budget items, such as time extensions, changes of scope or reductions in project scale, or budget moves of 10% or more? The document names a decision-maker only for the two cases it covers.
questions.quote: A recipient may need more time, may want to spend money on a different item, or may need to reduce the scale of the project.

questions.text: Records of approved grants and declined applications must be deleted after seven and two years, but the audit record must not be deletable by any user. Does deletion at the end of retention also remove the related audit history, declarations of interest and bank-change records? What retention applies to organisation records and to data held on organisations that never applied?
questions.quote: The system shall retain records of approved grants for seven years after the grant is closed and records of declined applications for two years after the decision, and shall then delete them.

questions.text: Who countersigns a grant agreement for the council, does this depend on the grant size or programme, and must the council's countersignature happen in the system?
questions.quote: No payment shall be made on a grant until the grant agreement has been signed by the recipient and countersigned by the council.

questions.text: How and how often does the system learn that an organisation's registration shows it as removed, dissolved or in insolvency? Is the register checked at payment creation, on a schedule, or by feed? Is the check also made for organisations without a charity or company number?
questions.quote: The system shall stop a payment request automatically if the recipient organisation's charity or company registration shows it as removed, dissolved or in insolvency.

questions.text: Accounts are treated as expired after 18 months, but programme managers want small organisations below an income threshold to be exempt, and the threshold is unset. Is the exemption in or out of the requirements, and what is the threshold? What happens to an application if accounts have expired and a new version is not uploaded?
questions.quote: Programme managers have suggested that small organisations with an annual income below a threshold should not have to provide accounts, but the threshold has not been set.

questions.text: What expiry rule applies to the governing document, safeguarding policy and equality policy? Only accounts have a stated expiry period, so an expiry date cannot be calculated for the others. Who sets it, and what happens to open applications when a document expires?
questions.quote: The system shall record an expiry date for each organisation document and shall ask the organisation to upload a new version when one expires.

questions.text: Youth Voice panel members under 18 may be unable to take part in decisions recorded in the system, and Legal Services have not decided. Until then, who is recorded as decision-maker for Youth Voice grants and how do under-18 panel members log in and take part?
