questions.quote: The Youth Voice fund panel includes young people who are under 18. Legal Services are considering whether they can take part in decisions recorded in the system or whether an adult must record the decision for them.

questions.text: What does 'quick to complete for small grants' mean? 'Small grants' is not defined, and the only measurable target is 30 minutes for grants under 1,000. Is that the only target, or are there others for larger small grants?
questions.quote: The application process should be quick to complete for small grants.

questions.text: How is the 'date by which a decision is expected' calculated for the acknowledgement email? Is it set per round, per programme (e.g. ten working days for Small Sparks), or entered by officers?
questions.quote: When an application is submitted the system shall send the applicant an acknowledgement by email with a reference number and the date by which a decision is expected.

questions.text: How do external auditors sign in? Council users use single sign-on and applicants and external assessors use email, password and a second factor, but external auditors and the ward members' access are not covered, though section 2.3 lists external auditors as users.
questions.quote: Council users shall sign in with the council's single sign-on, and applicants and external assessors shall sign in with an email address, a password and a second factor.

questions.text: How are monitoring due dates set (from agreement signing, project start, or the payment schedule)? When is the 'mid-point' for grants of 5,001 to 25,000, and on what dates are quarterly reports due?
questions.quote: Recipients of grants from 5,001 to 25,000 submit a mid-point report and an end-of-grant report.

questions.text: Equality information must not be visible to assessors or decision-makers, yet reports must break down applications by it. Which roles may see these reports, and at what level of aggregation (to avoid identifying individuals)?
questions.quote: The system shall report the applications received, approved and declined in each round, with the reasons for declining, by ward and by the equality information applicants provided.

questions.text: Small Sparks is open all year, but the system is built on rounds with opening and closing dates and a rule that no application is accepted after closing. How should open-all-year programmes be modelled, and how do the round budget and closing rules apply to them?
questions.quote: The fund is open all year, and decisions are made within ten working days.

questions.text: How are in-progress grants from other programmes handled at go-live? Only status, amount, organisation and programme are migrated for them, yet they may have outstanding payments, agreements and monitoring reports. Is multi-year or in-flight funding outside Strategic Partnerships to be managed in the new system or elsewhere?
questions.quote: Grants made in the three financial years before go-live shall be migrated into the system with their organisation, amount, programme and status, so that reports of funding to an organisation are complete.

questions.text: How is it checked that the two people connected with an organisation are 'not related to each other', and what counts as related (family, household, marriage)? Is a declaration enough, or is evidence required?
questions.quote: The requirement for two unrelated people follows the council's grants policy, which does not fund organisations controlled by a single family.

questions.text: Is the due diligence list exhaustive? 'Includes' suggests other checks. What other checks apply, do they vary by programme or grant size, and is due diligence needed for Ward Member Grants and Small Sparks?
questions.quote: Due diligence includes checking the organisation's accounts, its governing document and, for grants over 25,000, a credit check.

questions.text: Should ward members be notified when an organisation in their ward applies to any programme? The document says no decision has been made, so the requirement cannot be built or tested.
questions.quote: Some ward members have asked to be told when an organisation in their ward applies to any programme; no decision has been made.
